newsitem.title: USA: Light sweet cash crude dives on Brent barrage late.
newsitem.headline: Light sweet cash crude dives on Brent barrage late.

text.p: U.S. light sweet cash crude for April dove in Monday afternoon trading amid a barrage of offers of North Sea Brent crude on the Gulf Coast, traders said.
"The back month fell off because of the perception of all the Brents," one Gulf Coast trader said.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus 57 cents a barrel, down steeply from minus 10 cents earlier in the day.
Most traders were wrapping up last minute April deals ahead of pipeline scheduling on Tuesday.
May WTI/Cushing continued to shrink at $21.00-10 a barrel, down 20 cents from early afternoon amid plentiful supplies.
The April/May roll was talked flat in the aftermarket, after trading at plus 15 and 18 cents a barrel.
Among other grades, WTI/Midland was around minus 30-22 cents a barrel, steady with this morning.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was weaker at a $1.00 discount.
West Texas Sour/Midland was around $2.45-40 a barrel, up 10-20 cents from this morning as traders sought last-minute balance before May business gets underway.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was around $1.75-80 cents a barrel.
Trading is expected to subside after tomorrow's scheduling as many traders seek to hang up their hats until after the East holiday this weekend.
NYMEX and the IPE are closed on Friday to observe Good Friday. The IPE is also shut on Monday, the day after Easter.
